Ransomware Attack Hits Vietnam Construction Materials Firms, Disrupts Operations

A cyber attack has struck several leading companies in Vietnam’s Construction Materials industry, with ransomware crippling IT systems and causing significant operational disruption. Among the affected firms is Easterns AHP Minerals JSC, a major supplier of cement and aggregates, whose production sites have reportedly been hampered by the ongoing incident.

The attack, first detected late Tuesday, has forced multiple companies to shut down parts of their digital infrastructure, halting order processing and suspending some on-site operations. According to a spokesperson from the Vietnam Construction Materials Association (VCMA), “Many of our members are facing severe difficulties accessing their systems. Key processes, from inventory management to dispatch, are currently offline. This is impacting daily output and worker routines.”

At Easterns AHP Minerals JSC’s main plant in Binh Duong, employees were instructed to revert to manual procedures where possible, but sources say production volumes have dropped sharply. “We’re doing our best to maintain safety and keep essential lines running, but without our IT support, we’re severely limited,” said a plant supervisor who requested anonymity.

While the full scale of the attack remains unclear, initial assessments estimate that several hundred workers across the industry are affected by the disruption, with shifts shortened or rescheduled due to halted operations. Local trade union representative Tran Minh Chau expressed concern for employees’ livelihoods: “Many workers rely on steady shifts. We urge the companies to support staff while these issues are resolved.”

Industry analysts note that the Construction Materials sector has become increasingly reliant on digital systems for logistics and production planning. “This incident highlights the urgent need for robust cybersecurity,” commented Nguyen Van Quoc of VietSec Advisors.

As of Wednesday afternoon, technical teams were still working to contain the attack and restore operations. No timeline for full recovery has yet been provided.
